messages:
sam_infra: ap-northeast1 GPU pool 3 is stalled — provisioning held for ~12m. IOPS on local NVMe spiked and janitor backlog increased 6x. noticed a bunch of overlayfs orphan inodes and fsync storms. GPUs waiting on attach. anyone oncall? :eyes:
lauren_sre: seeing the same. scheduler shows attach retries due to node state 'io-wait'. can we pause janitor for that pool?
prashant_ops: pausing janitor is ok for short window. what's the error stream? paste dmesg/log tail pls.
sam_infra: tail from one affected node:
```
[ 1234.567890] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
[ 1234.568001] overlayfs: upperdir chown failed: -5
[ 1235.001200] fsync:  writeback_kthread blocked for 5000ms
[ 1236.112300] nvme nvme0: I/O 0xabc timed out, qid 1
```
marta_eng: that looks like write-amplification + stuck cleaner loop. could be metadata churn from many small deletes. any recent rollout of cleaner/trim?
lauren_sre: we rolled cleaner v2 last week into canary, but not ap-northeast1. cleaner runs via cron every 5m with concurrency 16. backlog noticed at 20k objs queued.
prashant_ops: ops-bot shows janitor concurrency exhausted in region ap-northeast1: "janitor-queue length=20345 concurrency=16 rate=0.3/s". I'll bump concurrency to 40 temporarily and throttle smallwrite batch size.
ops-bot: Temporary action: bumped janitor concurrency in ap-northeast1 from 16 -> 40 by prashant_ops at 11:42 UTC. Monitoring IOPS and attach queue.
sam_infra: thanks. also marking nodes with repeated nvme timeout to readonly. how many drives are at SMART reallocated > 100?
prashant_ops: quick query: `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1 | grep Reallocated` shows 3 nodes >100, 12 nodes >10. Not yet catastrophic but correlated with high fsync.
marta_eng: immediate mitigations: 1) pause high-churn cleanup jobs (tempfile sweeper) for that pool 2) kick janitor concurrency up 3) route new GPU attaches to dedicated reserve pool in ap-northeast1 for 30m 4) schedule rolling reboot of 4 worst nodes after drain
lauren_sre: agree. also enable prefix KV cache for common model workloads to reduce small writes. can we flip routing quickly?
sam_infra: routing flip in 2min -> redirect attach requests matching label `gpu:batch` to dedicated-reserve-apne1. Doing canary 10% first.
ops-bot: Route update: 10% traffic shifted to dedicated-reserve-apne1 by sam_infra.
prashant_ops: I/O graphs: write_iops baseline 18k -> 120k at spike, avg latency up to 40ms. After bumping janitor concurrency, iops down to 60k and attach queue reduced by ~30% so far.
marta_eng: follow-ups: - run `fsck -n` on flagged nodes overnight, prepare replacement drives for nodes >100 reallocated - investigate overlayfs inode leak in tempdir cleaner PR (#4221) - add soft rate limit on janitor enqueue per namespace to avoid global surges
lauren_sre: cost note: routing to dedicated reserve increases per-attach latency but avoids SLA breaches. ops: estimate incremental cost for 30m fallback?
prashant_ops: rough calc: 30m of reserve usage ~ $1.2k. still cheaper than rollback + customer impact if we keep mounts failing.
sam_infra: assigning actions: @marta_eng follow overlayfs/cleaner PR, @prashant_ops schedule reboots + drive replacements, @lauren_sre monitor attach SLOs and rollback routing if any regressions.
lauren_sre: ack. I'll watch SLO dashboard and set alert for attach latency > 500ms. :thumbsup:
prashant_ops: will follow up with ticket including node list + SMART dumps.
ops-bot: Incident note: ap-northeast1 ephemeral NVMe IOPS spike -> janitor backlog -> GPU attach holds. Status: mitigations applied (janitor concurrency bump, 10% route shift). Ops owners: prashant_ops, marta_eng.
sam_infra: closing loop for now, keeping thread open for next 2 hrs. if we see repeat spikes we'll revert cleaner changes and open incident pager. thanks all. :v:
